catalog:context:alcohol.description: NIAAA's Rethinking Drinking programme describes a printable four-week calendar card for recording individual drinks.

catalog:context:alcohol-free-day.description: A Harvard Health guide to Dry January describes using the Try Dry app to record drinking and personal goals.

catalog:context:nicotine.description: Smokefree.gov's quitSTART app includes tags for times or places associated with smoking urges as part of tracking a quit attempt.

catalog:context:sleep.description: The National Sleep Foundation's sleep diary has separate entries for waking and before bed, recorded daily.

catalog:exercise:bodyweight.description: An American Council on Exercise guide describes bodyweight sessions using exercises such as push-ups, squats, lunges and planks without external weights.

catalog:exercise:calisthenics.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes calisthenics as whole-body resistance exercises relying on body weight with little or no equipment.

catalog:exercise:cardio-zone2.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes Zone 2 cardio as moderate-intensity activity during which conversation remains possible, in contrast to higher-intensity zones.

catalog:exercise:climbing.description: A Climbing magazine article illustrates hangboard practice for particular grip positions alongside time spent climbing.

catalog:exercise:cycling.description: A cycling club guide describes group-riding calls such as 'car back' and 'car up', alongside hand signals for turns and road hazards.

catalog:exercise:functional-fitness.description: An American Council on Exercise guide describes functional sessions organised around combinations of movement patterns, including hinging, squatting, pushing and pulling.

catalog:exercise:hiit.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes HIIT sessions as repeated higher-intensity activity intervals alternated with lower-intensity recovery.

catalog:exercise:hiking.description: The American Hiking Society describes foot-only trails as one setting for hiking, managed for pedestrian travel away from motorised vehicles.

catalog:exercise:martial-arts.description: One Harvard Health guide describes a tai chi class combining a warm-up with instruction and practice of movement forms.

catalog:exercise:pilates.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes Pilates routines performed on a mat or on apparatus such as a reformer.

catalog:exercise:resistance-session.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes resistance sessions using free weights, machines or resistance bands, with muscles working against an external load.

catalog:exercise:rowing.description: Concept2's indoor rowing guide describes a four-part stroke: the catch, drive, finish and recovery.

catalog:exercise:running.description: The Road Runners Club of America describes run-walk-run sessions with alternating running and walking intervals, attributing the method to Jeff Galloway.

sourceOverride.title: What is U.S. Masters Swimming? - U.S. Masters Swimming

catalog:exercise:swimming.description: US Masters Swimming describes adult swimming clubs and workout groups organised through local swimming committees.

catalog:exercise:team-sport.description: A County Health Rankings description of adult recreational leagues lists soccer, softball, kickball and basketball at different playing levels.

catalog:exercise:walking.description: CDC's activity guide lists brisk walking as an example of moderate-intensity physical activity.

catalog:food-protocol:18-6.description: A Cleveland Clinic podcast includes an 18-hour daily fast among time-restricted eating patterns, corresponding to a six-hour eating window.

catalog:food-protocol:calorie-protein-ta.description: MyFitnessPal describes food logging that records calories and macronutrients, including protein, against personal goals.

catalog:food-protocol:carb-cycling.description: A Precision Nutrition guide describes carb cycling as alternating higher-carbohydrate workout days with lower-carbohydrate non-workout days.

catalog:food-protocol:carnivore.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes carnivore eating around meat, fish, eggs and limited dairy, excluding plant foods.

catalog:food-protocol:extended-fast.reason: The proposed source is a commercial fasting clinic's promotional page; its supporting excerpt makes benefit claims rather than independently documenting the proposed community routine.

catalog:food-protocol:low-carb.description: A Diet Doctor guide distinguishes stricter ketogenic eating from moderate and more liberal low-carbohydrate patterns.

catalog:food-protocol:omad.description: A Healthline guide describes one-meal-a-day eating as concentrating daily food intake into one meal rather than several meals.

catalog:food-protocol:vegan.description: The Vegan Society describes vegan eating as excluding animal-derived foods, including meat, fish, dairy, eggs and honey.

catalog:food-protocol:vegetarian.description: The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics describes lacto-ovo vegetarian eating as including dairy and eggs alongside plant foods while excluding meat, poultry and fish.

catalog:recovery:acupuncture.description: A Kaiser Permanente patient guide describes an acupuncture appointment with dimmed lights, quiet music and the practitioner checking on the person's comfort.

catalog:recovery:compression.description: The Conversation reports recovery boots used by athletes and wellness businesses, with inflatable sleeves applying pressure sequentially from the ends of the limbs towards the trunk.

catalog:recovery:float-tank.description: A Cleveland Clinic guide describes float therapy in a dark, quiet tank with a shallow pool of salt-saturated water.

catalog:recovery:hyperbaric-oxygen.description: Harvard Health reports some treatment centres marketing hyperbaric oxygen for uses beyond FDA-cleared indications, distinguishing those claims from established medical uses.

catalog:recovery:massage.description: An American Massage Therapy Association account of post-event sports massage describes lighter strokes such as compression and effleurage with passive stretching, rather than deep massage.

catalog:recovery:red-light.description: Cleveland Clinic describes red light therapy promoted at beauty salons, gyms and wellness centres as well as in medical-office and at-home contexts.

catalog:recovery:sauna.description: Finland's living-heritage register describes sauna bathing traditionally on Saturdays, with the practice now spread across other days too.

catalog:recovery:screen-curfew.reason: The quoted timing is a CDC expert recommendation, not a report of an observed community routine.

catalog:supplement:berberine.description: Memorial Sloan Kettering's reference describes berberine-containing plants used in traditional Chinese medicine and Ayurveda; this records traditional use, not established clinical benefit.
